description: Cross-reactivity and shared immunogenic epitope safety invariants

rules.message: Potential beta-lactam cross-reactivity: Documented penicillin hypersensitivity presents shared 1st-generation cephalosporin risk (1-3% cross-reactivity). Clinician evaluation recommended before ordering.

provenance.source: JAMA Review of Beta-Lactam Allergies & AAAAI Guidelines
citations: Blumenthal KG, et al. Evaluation and Management of Penicillin Allergy: A Review. JAMA. 2019;321(2):188-199.
Khan DA, et al. Cephalosporin Allergy Practice Parameters. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2022.

rules.message: Sulfonamide antimicrobial cross-reactivity: Patient has documented allergy to sulfonamide antibiotics. Cross-reactivity between antimicrobial sulfonamides carries severe hypersensitivity risk.

provenance.source: New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) Sulfonamide Review
citations: Strom BL, et al. Absence of Cross-Reactivity between Sulfonamide Antibiotics and Others. N Engl J Med. 2003;349:1628-1635.

rules.message: Cross-sensitivity in Aspirin/NSAID hypersensitivity: Patients with severe aspirin sensitivity or AERD cross-react with non-selective COX-inhibiting NSAIDs, risking acute bronchospasm.

provenance.source: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (JACI)
citations: Stevenson DD, Szczeklik A. Clinical and pathologic perspectives on aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2006;118(4):773-786.
